cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Raise the Impossibility
cards.instruction: Answer every strange offer with a more committed version that you can still justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your invisible friend can bring her family to my wedding. Tell them I've set places beside me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They walk through walls when they're bored. Are you sure?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They can wander. I'll book a ballroom that follows them; my guests aren't missing cake because a wall got in the way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ballroom can split when they go different ways. Do you want that option?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take it, and order a cake that multiplies with the rooms. Everyone beside me gets the first slice; we'll need enough versions of me to cut them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 treats B2 doubt as a request to allow wandering, granting it while commissioning a moving room; A5 directs B4 option and raises it to duplicated hosting.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wall-walking causes A3 following room; B4 splitting causes A5 multiplying cake and hosts, preserving A1 places beside A.

relationship.evidence: B2 warns about guests leaving and B4 proposes a venue solution, making B a helpful participant rather than a sequence of vetoes.

heightening.evidence: A5 escalates B4 split rooms into multiple cakes and versions of A to honor A1 seating promise; commitment becomes personally larger.

specificity.evidence: A1 wedding invitation and assigned seats establish an inclusive host; B4 selectable room option is sufficient fantasy context.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 duplicated host follows the first-slice and beside-me promise; the line is longer but each extra commitment has a supplied cause.
